shadows.name: focus-field

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Navigation, input, and textarea state changes.

motion.name: state-standard
motion.purpose: Buttons, landing links, and directional icons.

motion.name: hero-copy-entrance
motion.purpose: One-time landing hero hierarchy entrance when reduced motion is not requested.

motion.name: hero-reader-entrance
motion.purpose: One-time documentation reader entrance when reduced motion is not requested.

motion.name: workspace-entrance
motion.purpose: Introduces the Workspace command hierarchy once; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: worker-stage-response
motion.purpose: Current-operation entrance that repeats only when its resolved worker stage or validated chapter boundary changes; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: worker-indeterminate-activity
motion.purpose: Continuous activity signal with no percentage meaning; the entire line is removed under reduced motion so a static segment cannot imply completion.

motion.name: reader-entrance
motion.purpose: One-time operational Wiki header, chapter navigation, and article entrance when reduced motion is not requested.

motion.name: reader-chapter-change
motion.purpose: Short article response after a chapter selection; content remains static under reduced motion.

motion.name: chat-request-response
motion.purpose: Binds a submitted repository and question to the arriving pending, failed, or completed request surface; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: chat-source-evidence
motion.purpose: Introduces only the source-path rows returned with a completed Chat answer; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: chat-indeterminate-activity
motion.purpose: Signals an unresolved Chat job without implying retrieval stage or percentage; motion stops under reduced-motion preference.

motion.name: architecture-entrance
motion.purpose: One-time hero, blueprint, and section continuity cues; connector drawing is explanatory only and all timing disappears under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
AutoWiki is a mint editorial world where a repository becomes planned chapters and then a navigable technical Wiki. Warm white reading surfaces sit inside a luminous sea-glass atmosphere, near-black type carries the hierarchy, and deep teal marks operational context. The Landing route leads with a centered promise and a large, authentic document window rather than a conventional copy-and-card split.

The interface is evidence-led rather than ornamental. Dense technical material stays approachable through clear grouping, generous section rhythm, compact monospace metadata, and product proof built directly from the checked-in Spoon-Knife fixture. Landing, Workspace, Wiki, Chat, and Architecture keep distinct compositions while sharing the mint, near-black, and Manrope foundation.
keyCharacteristics: Warm white and mint surfaces with near-black type.
Strong editorial hierarchy with technical, factual detail.
Deep teal for operational context; near-black for primary actions and selected navigation.
Truthful worker status with cyan operational signals and no invented completion data.
Border-led structure with quiet, exceptional elevation.
Authentic repository paths, chapters, diagrams, and product evidence.
Grounded Chat keeps each submitted repository and question visibly bound to one answer and its returned source paths.
A provenance-labeled Spoon-Knife sample reuses the production reader without calling the backend.

rules.name: The Restrained Indigo Rule
rules.body: Indigo is a decision signal, not the default decoration; reserve it for primary actions, focus, selected global navigation, and connective logic that cyan cannot carry clearly.

rules.name: The White-and-Cyan Rule
rules.body: Reading white belongs inside the icy-cyan canvas and pale cyan fields so sections remain visible without beige warmth, heavy gray blocks, or cyan flooding the page.

rules.name: The Product-Is-The-Hero Rule
rules.body: The generated document remains the largest and most concrete object in the Landing first viewport; atmosphere, copy, and motion support it rather than compete with it.

rules.name: The Mobile Recomposition Rule
rules.body: At phone widths, remove secondary context and restack the reading flow instead of shrinking a desktop multi-rail layout until its text becomes ornamental.

rules.name: The Identity Display Rule
rules.body: Manrope identifies the product, generated document, or current operational state; body copy, navigation, controls, and dense workspace UI remain Segoe.

rules.name: The Metadata Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use monospace sparingly where literal paths, code, sequence, or repository structure make the interface more trustworthy.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with surface tone and a one-pixel rule before adding elevation; shadows must explain physical separation, not decorate a container.

rules.name: The Honest Activity Rule
rules.body: The continuous line is an indeterminate activity signal, never a completion meter. The current-operation panel enters once and repeats its restrained 240ms response only when its resolved worker stage or validated chapter boundary changes; under reduced motion, remove the line entirely and show the same status content statically so no frozen segment can be mistaken for a percentage.

rules.name: The Bound Evidence Rule
rules.body: Each Chat submission keeps its submitted repository and question attached to the pending state, final Markdown answer, and only the source paths the service actually returns; draft edits cannot rewrite the active request.

rules.name: The One Reader Rule
rules.body: Live jobs and verified samples use the same chapter navigation, Markdown, diagram, responsive, and accessibility behavior; sample-specific UI is limited to provenance and calls to generate a new Wiki.

rules.name: The Purposeful Motion Rule
rules.body: Animate the relationship a user needs to notice—never the whole interface merely because GSAP is available.

dos: Do put authentic repository paths, chapter names, diagrams, and generated output at the center of product proof.
Do use borders, tonal surfaces, and spacing as the primary hierarchy tools.
Do preserve Manrope for landing displays, generated-document identity, and operational state headings, with Segoe for body copy and controls.
Do keep interactive targets at least 2.75rem high with visible keyboard focus.
Do provide purpose-built desktop and mobile compositions and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Do share the real worker status between Workspace and `/wiki`, preserving its five backend-reported boundaries and factual chapter counts.
Do preserve the one-to-one binding between a Chat submission, its Markdown answer, and the actual source paths returned for that request.
Do render the verified Spoon-Knife sample through the shared production Wiki reader and keep its provenance and zero-call behavior explicit.
Do treat Landing, Workspace, Wiki, Chat, and Architecture as distinct modes of one connected repository-to-chapters-to-Wiki journey.
donts: Don't turn AutoWiki into a generic chatbot visual language; the structured wiki is the flagship artifact.
Don't flood screens with indigo, gradients, decorative glow, or unsupported AI spectacle.
Don't use large shadows where a one-pixel border or cool surface change already defines structure.
Don't introduce oversized pills or corner radii beyond the established compact document geometry.
Don't fabricate metrics, testimonials, repositories, progress states, or product capabilities as visual filler.
Don't turn indeterminate Wiki activity into a percentage, elapsed-time estimate, completion forecast, or reduced-motion segment that looks like progress.
Don't present grounded Chat as a conversational transcript, infer missing citations, or let draft edits relabel an in-flight or completed request.
Don't let sample mode submit a job, call a backend/provider, hide its provenance, or drift into a separate reader implementation.
Don't generalize the Architecture blueprint's accepted grid-pattern detector advisory to unrelated surfaces.
Don't add ambient GSAP choreography; every motion must clarify entrance, state change, navigation continuity, or evidence arrival and must disappear safely under reduced motion.
